Figure 2:Sensitivity to the focal length.An in-domain frame under its original camera and with the video and
intrinsics rescaled by 0.60. ViDiHand and ACE-Ego-Hand, which regress the depth, misplace the 3D hands after rescaling, while
ViDiHand2 stays closest to the ground truth. Insets show the mesh overlays.

Figure 3:Overview of ViDiHand2.The Multi-Level Latent Encoder and the Hand Latent Decoder turn the input clip into video features
and hand and joint tokens. In autoregressive (AR) rollouts, each chunk also attends to the key-value (KV) cache of the previous chunk.
The Joint-Heatmap Refiner predicts the 2D joint locations, and MANO gives the posed hand. Fine-Grained Geometric Lifting places this
hand in camera coordinates, and Confidence-Gated Fusion fuses it with the 2D locations. In the bottom row, the refiner blends heat-map
and regressed locations. The lifting fits the depthZtZ_{t}at which the joint pairs on the rays keep their MANO distancesLt,bL_{t,b}.
Clip-Level Ray Fitting adds a temporal constraint. The fusion blends the joints on the rays and the MANO joints with a gategjg_{j}.

Figure 4:Confidence-Gated Fusion on a hand truncated by the image border.Projected joints of the variants ofTab.8and the ground truth, shown in gray, with mean 2D errors. The checkerboard lies beyond the image. The fusion follows the 2D location
where the MANO finger leaves the image finger in the orange box, and keeps the MANO hand beyond the border in the red box.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison in the wild on Gen-HumanEgo.MANO overlays, where a visible hand without a mesh is a
detection failure. Insets: the hands in 3D with 10 s wrist paths, with the ground truth in light colors.
Top: a left hand behind a shoe, which HaWoR, ViDiHand and ACE-Ego-Hand misplace. Middle: the hands open a drawer and take something
out, with the right hand in dim light. HaWoR misplaces the right hand, ACE-Ego-Hand both hands and ViDiHand the left hand. Bottom: at a basket,
HaWoR puts the left hand on the right leg and ViDiHand draws the right one far too large. WiLoR fails to detect one hand in every row. ViDiHand2 places both hands correctly.

Figure 6:Qualitative comparison in the wild on Ego4D[13], EgoDex[15]and Xperience[53].Without reliable ground
truth, the overlays show image alignment only. Top: hands in a plant. Middle: a tray and a rake. Bottom: a phone. WiLoR
places the left hand on the leg in the top row and fails to detect the right hand in the other two. HaWoR detects only one hand in the top row,
mis-poses the right hand in the middle row, fails to detect both hands at the phone and puts a right hand on the floor. ViDiHand and ACE-Ego-Hand draw the hands one size too large in the top row and misplace or mis-pose a hand in the other two. ViDiHand2 aligns with the image
in every row.

Figure S1:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Top:Both hands work on a woven basket on the lap. WildHands brings the two hands too close together, while InterWild produces long outlying wrist paths. EgoForce and HandFlow fail to detect the current right hand. HaWoR shows a large trajectory excursion, InfiniHand produces dense long outlying paths, and ViDiHand shifts the right hand far from the ground truth. ViDiHand2 keeps both hands and wrist paths close to the ground truth.Bottom:Both hands handle small objects over a pot near a window. Hamba overlaps the current hands, HandDGP and PAD-Hand send the right-wrist path far downward, while InterWild produces dense back-and-forth wrist excursions. EgoForce has a long right-wrist outlier, and InfiniHand produces wide lateral left-wrist excursions. HaWoR also shows large trajectory excursions. ViDiHand2 keeps both hands and the trajectory shape closer to the ground truth.

Figure S2:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Top:Both hands wash a blender cup over a kitchen sink. Hamba, AnyHand and EgoForce produce long wrist-path outliers. HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, PAD-Hand and Dyn-HaMR extend the right-hand path far above the ground-truth motion. HaWoR adds repeated large excursions around the hands. ViDiHand2 follows the compact ground-truth wrist paths and the current two-hand arrangement.Middle:Both hands wring cloths over a purple basin and hang them on a metal towel rail. InterWild and EgoForce produce long outlying wrist paths. HaMeR and OmniHands add large excursions across the scene, while HandDGP produces long left-wrist outliers and Dyn-HaMR produces jittery wrist paths. HaWoR separates the current hands too far. ViDiHand2 places both hands close to the ground truth with fewer large path deviations.Bottom:Both hands reach into an open drawer. Hamba omits the current left hand and produces long wrist-path outliers. WildHands and InterWild shift the left hand toward the center, while AnyHand brings both hands too close together. Dyn-HaMR misorients the left hand, and HaWoR produces jittery wrist paths. ViDiHand2 follows the ground-truth hand arrangement and the more compact motion paths.

Figure S3:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands sort small items beside a bag on a round table. Hamba omits the current left hand. InterWild shifts the left-hand trajectory and the current left hand far from the ground truth, while EgoForce adds long outliers for both wrists. HaWoR shows large repeated motion excursions. PAD-Hand spreads the right-wrist path laterally, and InfiniHand sends the left path far across the scene. ViDiHand2 keeps the hands and their motion paths closer to the ground-truth region.

Figure S5:Top:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands hold a woven basket over the lap. AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and HandFlow fail to detect the right hand. InterWild, PAD-Hand, Dyn-HaMR and ViDiHand draw the right hand far too large, and HaWoR also enlarges it. HaWoR puts the left hand on the right leg. ViDiHand2 keeps both hands near the ground-truth size and grip locations.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands handle a cloth in a purple bowl. EgoForce produces a mesh that covers most of the image. WildHands displaces the left palm across the bowl, AnyHand, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and Dyn-HaMR misplace the overlapping hands, and HandDGP swaps them. InterWild shifts the right hand down the forearm. HaWoR separates the left hand from the contact region. ViDiHand2 follows the ground-truth hand size and the contact location above the cloth.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands pull the edge of a bedsheet. AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and PAD-Hand fail to detect the left hand despite its visible grip, and HaWoR places it far above on the bedsheet. ViDiHand2 reconstructs both hands at the sheet edge, with placement close to the ground truth.

Figure S6:Top:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands grip a small pouch over the lap. WildHands shows no hand meshes, and AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and PAD-Hand fail to detect the left hand. ViDiHand2 retains both hands and follows the ground-truth grip locations on either side of the pouch.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands hold a pot near a window. WildHands shows no hand meshes, and Hamba, AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and HandFlow fail to detect the left hand. EgoForce also enlarges the right hand and shifts it upward, and HaWoR moves the left hand beside the right. InterWild reconstructs it too large and extends it down the forearm. ViDiHand2 retains both hands at the pot rim, near their ground-truth placement.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.The left hand rests on a tray of blue tubes while the right hand gathers a bundle of lavender strands. EgoForce produces a mesh spanning much of the image. Hamba, AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, PAD-Hand and OmniHands place a right-hand mesh on the left hand and leave the right hand empty, while WildHands, HaMeR and HandFlow fail to detect the left hand. ViDiHand2 retains both hands at the tray and strands, with size and placement close to the ground truth.

Figure S7:Top:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.The left hand reaches toward scissors on a white cutting table while the right hand holds white fabric, between racks of clothing. EgoForce omits the right-hand overlay. WildHands, InterWild, AnyHand, HaMeR, Hamba, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and OmniHands spread the right-hand fingers beyond the visible grip. HaWoR displaces the right hand onto the tabletop. ViDiHand2 follows both hands.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands pack small parts into white bags at a cluttered workbench. WildHands and AnyHand elongate both hand meshes down the forearms, and Hamba, InterWild and OmniHands elongate the left-hand mesh. InfiniHand makes the same error more strongly, shifting the palm away from the visible hand. ViDiHand2 keeps the left palm and the right-hand grip closer to the ground truth.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands handle small test tubes beside papers on a laboratory bench. Hamba fails to detect both hands. WildHands and InterWild displace the left palm toward the foreground, while HaWoR shifts it sideways and misplaces the right hand. EgoForce raises the right-hand mesh above the visible grip. ViDiHand2 retains both hands near the ground-truth contact locations.

Figure S8:Top:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.The left hand touches a blue tube rack on a laboratory bench while the right hand is raised. Hamba fails to detect both hands, while HaWoR places both meshes on the right hand. EgoForce omits the left hand and, like InterWild, greatly enlarges the right hand. ViDiHand2 retains both hands with size and placement close to the ground truth.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Gen-HumanEgo.Both hands handle small objects above a round table. Hamba, AnyHand, HaMeR, WildHands and WiLoR make the left palm too broad and extend it down the wrist. ViDiHand2 better preserves the ground-truth palm size and the two manipulation locations.

Figure S10:Top:Qualitative comparison on Ego4D.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. Both hands wash an object in a sink. Hamba, EgoForce and PAD-Hand show no hand meshes, and AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and HandFlow omit the right hand. InterWild shifts the left hand onto the counter, while HaWoR separates the hands from the washing region. InfiniHand, ViDiHand and ACE-Ego-Hand draw both hands too large. ViDiHand2 keeps both meshes at the visible hand locations and image scale.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Ego4D.The left hand holds patterned fabric beside an ironing board while the right hand holds an iron. AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, PAD-Hand and HandFlow omit the left-hand overlay. InterWild places it far above the visible hand. InfiniHand, ViDiHand and ACE-Ego-Hand greatly enlarge both hands. ViDiHand2 follows the visible left-hand grip and the right hand holding the iron.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Ego4D.A hand reaches into a cluttered pile of tools and engine parts beside a scooter. AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, PAD-Hand and HandFlow omit the left-hand overlay. HaWoR shifts the left hand downward and rotates its fingers away from the visible reach. InfiniHand, ViDiHand and ACE-Ego-Hand enlarge the left hand beyond its image outline. ViDiHand2 follows the extended left hand and the partly visible right hand.

Figure S11:Top:Qualitative comparison on Ego4D.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. Both hands carry a round tray through a dim doorway. Hamba, AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, HandFlow and PAD-Hand omit the left-hand overlay. InfiniHand, ViDiHand and ACE-Ego-Hand enlarge the left hand beyond the visible grip. ViDiHand2 retains both hands at the tray rim, following the visible grip locations and hand scale.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Ego4D.The left hand holds a power tool against a mechanical assembly that the right hand steadies. Hamba shows no hand meshes, and EgoForce omits the right hand. HaWoR displaces and reverses the apparent hand locations. WildHands, InfiniHand and ACE-Ego-Hand enlarge the right hand, while ViDiHand extends it below the visible wrist. ViDiHand2 places both meshes over the hands beside the assembly.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Ego4D.Outdoors, the left hand holds a cup while the right hand holds a white plastic container. AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and PAD-Hand omit the left-hand overlay. InfiniHand places a large open hand below the visible cup grip, while HaWoR and HandFlow shift the left hand slightly away from the cup. ViDiHand2 follows both the cup-holding hand and the hand holding the container.

Figure S12:Top:Qualitative comparison on EgoDex.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. The left hand holds a small sand tray while the right hand holds a rake. Hamba and HaMeR place both meshes over the left hand, and WildHands, AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and HandFlow fail to detect the right hand. EgoForce adds two spurious arms from the top of the image. OmniHands and InfiniHand shift the right hand onto the tray, and HaWoR mis-poses it. InterWild makes the left hand much too large, and ViDiHand and ACE-Ego-Hand misplace or mis-pose a hand. ViDiHand2 follows the tray-holding hand and the visible rake grip.Middle:Qualitative comparison on EgoDex.On a yellow surface, the left hand wipes a flat case with a cloth while the right hand holds it. WildHands and MINT enlarge the left hand, and WildHands also fails to detect the right hand. InterWild places an oversized right hand across the wiping hand, while EgoForce produces fragmented meshes far beyond both hands. HaWoR overlaps both predictions on the supporting hand, and ViDiHand enlarges the left hand and extends the right wrist down the forearm. ViDiHand2 follows both the wiping hand and the supporting grip at the visible scale.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on EgoDex.Both hands rest on a stack of paper, the right hand holding a small transparent object. Hamba and HaMeR omit the left-hand overlay and place an extra mesh on the right hand, and InterWild enlarges the left hand. WildHands overlaps a large left-hand mesh with the right hand, while OmniHands also merges both predictions at the right grip. Dyn-HaMR also omits the left hand. ViDiHand2 places the left hand on the page and follows the right-hand grip on the object.

Figure S13:Top:Qualitative comparison on EgoDex.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. Both hands hold a chessboard at its near edges. Hamba shows no hand meshes, and HaMeR, HandFlow, PAD-Hand and ACE-Ego-Hand fail to detect the right hand at the image edge. WildHands and OmniHands overlap both predictions near the left hand, while EgoForce produces an oversized mesh above the board. Dyn-HaMR shifts the left hand inward and rotates the right palm toward the camera. ViDiHand2 follows the two visible hands at the board edges.Middle:Qualitative comparison on EgoDex.Both hands work with green fabric on a table. Hamba omits the right-hand mesh, while AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, PAD-Hand and HandFlow omit the left. EgoForce produces a large mesh covering the right side of the image. InterWild extends both wrists, and HaWoR separates and reverses the apparent hand locations. ViDiHand2 follows both visible hands on the fabric.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.The left hand is held open next to a phone and the right hand holds the phone. Several detect-then-reconstruct baselines, including Hamba, HandDGP, WiLoR and PAD-Hand, fail to detect the right hand and place a right-hand mesh far above it, and EgoForce shows no right hand. HaMeR overlays neither visible hand and places its meshes far up the frame. HaWoR fails to detect both hands, putting one mesh on the floor above the phone and one on the leg. ViDiHand draws the right hand on the screen, and ACE-Ego-Hand spreads its fingers over the phone. ViDiHand2 aligns with both hands.

Figure S14:Top:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. A person cuts paper with scissors at a shared table. Hamba, HaMeR and Dyn-HaMR place meshes on another person’s hand, and Hamba also puts a left-hand mesh on the scissor-holding hand. WildHands places the left-hand mesh on the other person’s hand, while OmniHands moves both meshes above the scissors. HaWoR places a hand near the other person’s face, and ViDiHand shifts the right hand away from the scissors. ViDiHand2 follows the paper-holding hand and the scissor grip.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.A person marks a grid while holding the sheet flat. Most image-based baselines, including Hamba, InterWild, AnyHand, HaMeR, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and OmniHands, make the left hand much too large. HaWoR places a right-hand mesh over the visible left hand and omits the writing-hand overlay. InfiniHand overlaps an open right-hand mesh with the left hand, while ViDiHand makes the left hand too small. ViDiHand2 follows the left-hand spread and the right-hand pen grip.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.A person marks small cards with a pen. Hamba omits the left-hand mesh, while EgoForce omits the right. InterWild enlarges and separates both hands, and HaWoR produces a large mesh covering the foreground. InfiniHand makes the right hand much too large. ViDiHand2 places both hands at the card and pen grip.

Figure S15:Top:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. Both hands hold a vertical cardboard piece. HaWoR shows no hand meshes. Hamba, InterWild, OmniHands, AnyHand, HaMeR, EgoHandICL and WiLoR enlarge the right hand beyond the visible grip, while ViDiHand makes both hands too small. ViDiHand2 preserves both grips despite the long nails.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Both hands twist a lid on a dark container. Several baselines, e.g., Hamba and AnyHand, extend the right hand beyond the visible wrist, and InterWild stretches the left hand down the forearm. HaWoR separates the left hand from the container, and ViDiHand makes the left grip too small. ViDiHand2 keeps both meshes around the container and follows the visible lid grip.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.A person holds a ruler against cardboard with the left hand and a red tool with the right. Hamba omits the right-hand overlay, while HaWoR shows neither hand. HandDGP and OmniHands enlarge the left hand beyond its visible outline. InterWild, HaMeR, AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and OmniHands extend the right-hand mesh above the visible grip. ViDiHand2 follows the supporting left hand and the right-hand grip.

Figure S16:Top:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. A person reaches toward items on a shelf. Hamba omits the left-hand overlay, while HaWoR shows neither hand. EgoForce shifts the left hand to the right of the visible reach. InfiniHand enlarges and lowers it, and MINT shifts the right hand inward from the visible fist. ViDiHand2 follows the reaching hand and the right fist.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Both hands handle tools and cardboard on a table. EgoForce shows no meshes. HaWoR greatly enlarges and separates both hands, while Dyn-HaMR displaces the right hand to the lower-right image edge. MINT enlarges the right hand, and InfiniHand makes the left hand too broad. ViDiHand2 follows both visible hand positions at the work surface.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.A person cuts cardboard with a utility knife while holding it flat. AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, PAD-Hand and HandFlow omit the right-hand overlay. HaWoR places both meshes at the left hand instead of the knife grip. EgoForce shifts the right hand upward and left, while Hamba and HaMeR stretch it down the forearm. ViDiHand2 follows the supporting palm and the knife-holding hand.

Figure S17:Top:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. A person holds a yellow packet while reaching toward shelf items. HaWoR shows no hand meshes, and Hamba, AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and PAD-Hand omit the left-hand overlay. InterWild shifts it away from the packet, while OmniHands makes it much too large and extends it up the shelf. ViDiHand2 follows the packet-holding hand and the right-hand reach.Middle:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Both hands manipulate small pieces beside a cardboard pattern. Hamba overlaps both meshes on the right hand, and HaMeR and WildHands omit the left-hand overlay. EgoForce greatly enlarges it over the work surface, while Dyn-HaMR also makes it too large. HaWoR omits the left hand and shrinks the right, and OmniHands shifts the left hand across the phone. ViDiHand2 follows both hands at their separate working positions.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Both hands sort small white pieces on a table. Hamba omits the right-hand mesh. WildHands, HaMeR and OmniHands overlap both predictions at the visible left hand. HaWoR puts a right-hand mesh there and omits the other hand. AnyHand, EgoHandICL, WiLoR and InterWild greatly enlarge the right hand. ViDiHand2 follows both hands at their separate positions among the pieces.

Figure S18:Top:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.Without reliable ground truth, the overlays show image alignment only. A person holds puzzle pieces in the left palm while reaching across a shared table. Hamba, HaMeR, EgoForce, HaWoR and HandFlow omit the left-hand overlay. HaMeR places a mesh on another person’s hand, while HaWoR shifts the right hand upward onto the pen holder. InterWild shifts the left hand onto the table, and InfiniHand spreads its fingers beyond the visible palm. ViDiHand2 follows the piece-holding palm and the right-hand reach.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Xperience.The left hand rests on a sheet while the right hand reaches toward small cut blocks. Hamba, AnyHand, EgoForce, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, PAD-Hand and HandFlow fail to detect the right hand. Hamba, AnyHand, HaMeR and InterWild also elongate the left wrist into the foreground. HaWoR overlaps both meshes at the left hand, and Dyn-HaMR distorts the left palm. ViDiHand2 follows the supporting hand and the reaching right hand.

Figure S20:Top:Qualitative comparison on H2O.One hand rests over the other on a checkered cloth. Hamba fails to detect the right hand. AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL and WiLoR fail to detect the left. InterWild separates the hands, and EgoForce produces a single oversized mesh covering the image. ViDiHand2 recovers both hands near the ground-truth overlap.Middle:Qualitative comparison on HOT3D.A raised hand holds a small object beside a desk. Hamba, WildHands and HaMeR assign a left-hand mesh to the visible right hand. InterWild and OmniHands add an overlapping hand, while HaWoR also assigns a left-hand mesh to the right hand and adds a second hand near the mouse. ViDiHand2 retains the visible right hand and follows its position and grip.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on OakInk2.Both hands cooperate to twist a bottle cap. ViDiHand2 preserves the grasp and follows the visible finger contours more closely. InfiniHand enlarges the right hand and shifts it down and to the right, misaligning it with the cap.

Figure S21:Top:Qualitative comparison on Ego-Pro.Both hands hold a blue folder. WildHands, HaMeR and OmniHands omit both overlays. HaWoR shifts the left hand onto the folder. ViDiHand2 follows both grips, close to the ground truth.Bottom:Qualitative comparison on Ego-Std.Hands hold a bottle beside a sink and mirror. Hamba, WildHands, HaMeR and OmniHands place both meshes on the reflected hands, while AnyHand, HandDGP, EgoHandICL, WiLoR, HaWoR, PAD-Hand and Dyn-HaMR place the left-hand mesh on the reflection. InterWild shifts the left hand toward the sink and the right mesh down the forearm. ViDiHand2 follows the foreground hands around the bottle.

Figure S22:Thumb distance on a hand-held 20 cm ruler.The first row shows the input at four moments: 1, the left hand
behind the cup; 2, the ruler lifted and tilted; 3, the ruler upright; and 4, the right hand behind the cup. The other rows
follow the order of Tab.1, with ViDiHand2 last in a green border. Each frame shows the predicted thumb tips and the
scaled distance in cm. Under each name are the MAE, the percentage of frames within 1 cm and Det., the percentage of frames
with both hands detected. The plots show the scaled distance over the clip and print the values beyond the axis.
